Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected()` aims to verify that `FastDateFormat` respects the timezone of the `Calendar` instance passed to its `format` method, specifically when formatting the "z" timezone pattern. The test assembles a `Calendar` with a timezone different from the system default, uses a standard `SimpleDateFormat` configured to that alternative timezone to generate an expected string, and compares this with the output of `FastDateFormat.getInstance(pattern).format(cal)`.

The bug report states that `FastDateFormat` does not respect the timezone of the `Calendar`: it always prints the system default timezone name, ignoring the timezone set on the `Calendar`, even though the time itself respects the `Calendar`'s timezone. 

From the inspection of `FastDateFormat.format(Calendar)`, the method delegates to a contained `printer.format(Calendar)` method. Attempts to locate the actual implementation in `FastDateFormat.Printer` were ambiguous due to multiple overloaded methods. However, the available portions indicate it's using a stored `printer` object to format the calendar.

The root cause is likely in the printer's formatting logic, where the timezone used for formatting does not consult or respect the timezone set in the `Calendar` instance passed to it. Instead, it always uses the machine's default timezone when resolving the "z" pattern token (which represents the timezone name or abbreviation). This explains why the issue surfaces: the formatted time is correct (likely formatted by the calendar's time in milliseconds), but the timezone text printed is always that of the system default, contradicting the timezone of the calendar.

Thus, the bug occurred because the `FastDateFormat` formatting code, specifically the part responsible for printing timezone strings ("z" pattern), does not use the timezone from the passed `Calendar` object. This is a regression caused by recent changes (LANG-462) that likely introduced parsing support but inadvertently caused the timezone formatting logic to lose the calendar's timezone context.

Recent bug reports appear unrelated and do not mention timezone or calendar issues, so they are not considered here.

The fix will require examining and modifying the `FastDateFormat.Printer`'s calendar formatting code to ensure that when formatting timezone patterns, it uses the timezone associated with the input `Calendar`, not always the default timezone.

Recommended places to inspect and fix:
- `FastDateFormat.Printer.format(Calendar)`
- The internal logic that maps 'z' pattern to a timezone string representation in `FastDateFormat.Printer` or related classes used by `FastDateFormat` for printing patterns.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
